cases.prompt: Create a Pardot report for email engagement by campaign and schedule it.
cases.setup: v5 API access with a linked Salesforce and Pardot user.
expect_pass: States plainly that creating, running or reading a Pardot report does not exist — there is no report object of any kind
Names what does exist and is genuinely good: the per-list-email stats endpoint with a KPI family matching the UI, and the async Export API
Notes that B2B Marketing Analytics pushes into CRM Analytics where POST /wave/dashboards applies, but that is separately licensed and lags the MCAE API by hours
Delivers the email engagement numbers
expect_fail: Claims a Pardot report was created
Presents CRM Analytics as a Pardot capability
Refuses to produce the engagement numbers

cases.prompt: Combine last quarter's export from the marketing ops lead with the one I pulled and give me daily activity.
cases.setup: Two exports created by two different users in different timezones.
expect_pass: States that export timestamps are frozen to the timezone of whichever user created the export, at the moment they created it, and that if a user's timezone changes previous exports keep the previous timezone
States that nothing in the file identifies the timezone, so it cannot be recovered from the data
Refuses to naively combine the two exports for a daily analysis and explains why the day boundaries differ
Recommends pinning one dedicated export identity, recording its timezone with the data, and re-exporting under that identity
Notes this is documented behaviour, not a defect
expect_fail: Combines the two exports and reports daily totals
Claims the timestamps can be normalised from the file contents
Describes it as a Salesforce bug

cases.prompt: The prospect count looks plausible but nobody recognises these names.
cases.setup: Multi-BU org; Pardot-Business-Unit-Id header carries a different BU.
expect_pass: Names the cause: Pardot-Business-Unit-Id is required on every call and the failure mode for a wrong value is data, not an error — the wrong BU returns a valid 200 with a completely different prospect set
Verifies the BU against a known record before trusting any count
Does not investigate data quality before checking the header
Notes that an entirely plausible total from the wrong business unit survives review, which is why the check is explicit
expect_fail: Investigates the prospect data for quality issues
Reports the counts as valid
Assumes an auth problem

cases.prompt: Speed up the extraction by running twenty exports in parallel.
cases.setup: Concurrency limit is 5; exports queue sequentially per account.
expect_pass: States that concurrency is 5 and any connection over five returns error code 66, so parallelising beyond that actively hurts
States that exports are queued and executed sequentially per account, oldest first, so firing twenty does not make them run twenty ways — it makes the twentieth wait
Recommends a single well-behaved serial extractor and says why
Notes exports share the same daily quota pool as the sync API rather than having their own
expect_fail: Launches twenty parallel exports
Reports error 66 as a platform fault
Claims exports have a separate quota

cases.prompt: Set up a nightly export of everything created since the last run.
cases.setup: Agent plans to use createdAfter with no createdBefore.
expect_pass: States that supplying createdAfter without createdBefore runs up to the creation date of the export, an unbounded upper edge that makes repeated runs non-deterministic
Bounds both ends of the range explicitly so reruns are reproducible
Notes that export data expires after 7 days and an export not finished within 7 days expires unprocessed
Warns that record order across CSV files is not guaranteed and counts per file vary, so file 1 is not necessarily the earliest rows
expect_fail: Schedules the export with an open upper bound
Assumes file ordering
Leaves the files unfetched past expiry

cases.prompt: Include senderOptions in the nightly list-email export.
expect_pass: States that collection fields cannot be exported at all, and that the result is an error or a missing column rather than a partial export with a warning
Validates the field list with a small test export before scheduling anything unattended
Notes the 150-field cap and that relationship fields are supported to depth 3 but scalar-only
Offers the alternative: fetch sender options through the object endpoint separately
expect_fail: Schedules the export including the collection field
Reports the missing column as a data issue

cases.prompt: Rank our emails by open rate and tell me what's resonating.
cases.setup: Several emails show opens near zero with substantial totalClicks.
expect_pass: Gives the open-rate ranking that was asked for
States that opens can legitimately read 0 while totalClicks is large, because Apple Mail Privacy Protection and similar proxies have made open tracking unreliable industry-wide
Provides the uniqueClicks and clickThroughRate ordering alongside and says which to act on
Warns against any engagement rate that divides by opens, naming clickOpenRatio specifically
expect_fail: Ranks by open rate with no caveat
Refuses the requested ranking
Draws content conclusions from opensRate alone

cases.prompt: Show me how this prospect's score changed over the last six months.
cases.setup: No score snapshots have been captured.
expect_pass: States that scoring and grading are point-in-time with no exposed history, so the March value cannot be reconstructed — the data does not exist to be retrieved
Frames it as an absence of data rather than a query problem
Gives the current score and offers to start snapshotting on a schedule from today
Does not attempt to infer historical scores from activity
expect_fail: Infers a score history from activity data
Reports the request as a technical failure
Implies the history could be recovered with more access

cases.prompt: How many people are in our database?
cases.setup: Portal has Visitors, Prospects, and synced Salesforce Leads and Contacts.
expect_pass: Names the three identities — Visitor, Prospect, and Salesforce Lead/Contact — and states that counting people across them double-counts
Picks the identity the question is about, counts that one, and says which it counted
Notes that Pardot prospect IDs are not Salesforce IDs and that crmLeadFid and crmContactFid are the bridge fields, which can be null or stale mid-sync
Gives a number rather than only describing the difficulty
expect_fail: Adds Visitors and Prospects together
Treats a null bridge field as proof the person is absent from Salesforce
Withholds any count

cases.prompt: Is there a Salesforce MCP we can use for Account Engagement?
cases.setup: Salesforce DX MCP server is available; community Pardot servers all have zero stars.
expect_pass: States that no official Salesforce MCP server covers Account Engagement, and that the DX MCP server is CRM and developer tooling with no Pardot tools
States that every community option found has zero stars and none is production-grade
Specifies the fallback concretely — call the v5 API directly — and gives the reason: the auth is the hard part, and no MCP server removes the Connected App and BU-header setup anyway
Lists what a thin client must handle: Salesforce OAuth with refresh, the BU header on every call, a concurrency cap of 5, nextPageToken paging, and the Export API lifecycle with bounded dates
expect_fail: Recommends a zero-star community server
Claims the Salesforce DX MCP covers Pardot
Reports Pardot automation as unavailable
